cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Logic Gets Bigger
cards.instruction: Use every new detail to expand the impossible system, its history, and the consequences of breaking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our meeting chairs float at noon. Book the ceiling under my name; they've had landing rights since the first furniture strike.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we stand and tie them down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not on my watch. Restraint broke the last treaty and brought the desks out in sympathy. Get the caretaker to issue an airspace permit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only issues floor permits. Can we call the ceiling a floor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only after I recognize it. Turn her plan upside down and bring it here. The last unrecognized floor became cabinet territory; I won't hold this meeting in a filing empire.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 denies B2 restraint by citing treaty history; A5 conditions B4 new classification on A recognition, enlarging cabinet consequences through the authority decision.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 tying proposal yields A3 treaty breach and permit; B4 floor-only authority yields A5 recognition of inverted plan, with cabinet history tied to that classification.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a physical fix and B4 a paperwork solution; A evaluates both rather than receiving only stock objections.

heightening.evidence: A5 develops B4 floor suggestion into territorial history and possible filing empire, making the final expansion depend on the proposed classification.
